entries.note: He doesn't say which theories, apart from the Google-search example, or what counts as fizzling out, so readers would test this in different ways.

entries.test: Google's global search-engine market share (e.g. StatCounter) in November 2022 compared with November 2024.
entries.note: 'All that much' is vague, but most readers would agree on the plain reading of a small change in share.

entries.test: Late-2024 surveys of large-enterprise executives on whether generative AI deployments met their expectations.
entries.note: The context reads as generative AI generally, not just the ChatGPT product. The clause about high-school students was left out.

entries.test: 2024 industry and analyst reports on how many enterprise generative-AI pilots reached documented, measurable production success.
entries.note: 'Relatively few' is vague but has a plain reading.
These are his own words from the January 2023 Klein interview, which he reprints and stands by. Whether a system has a 'conception of truth' has no shared test.

entries.test: Published hallucination-rate benchmarks for ChatGPT and other frontier models from 2023 through late 2024.
entries.note: The exact words quoted are the others' projection; his own assertion is the next line, 'They didn't.' Elsewhere in the post he grants that hallucinations may have declined.

entries.test: Whether frontier LLMs, including RAG-based systems, still produced measurable hallucinations on factuality benchmarks in late 2024.
Whether any scaled, RAG-based or prompt-mitigated LLM had a near-zero hallucination rate on public benchmarks as of November 2024.
Hallucination and fabrication rates of ChatGPT in late 2022 compared with its 2024 versions on public factuality benchmarks.
entries.note: This conflicts with his own later concession that hallucinations 'may have declined'.

entries.test: Whether 2024 benchmarks and audits show hallucinations occurring routinely in frontier LLM outputs.
Whether frontier LLMs still had non-zero hallucination rates on public benchmarks in late 2024.
entries.note: Only the firm part ('haven't vanished') can be graded; 'may have declined' is a hedge.

entries.test: Factuality and hallucination benchmark scores of GPT-3.5 at launch compared with leading models in November 2024.
entries.note: 'Wishing and hoping' is rhetoric; the substantive claim is that factuality has barely changed.

entries.test: Whether LLMs using RAG, larger scale or system-prompt mitigations still hallucinated on public benchmarks in late 2024.
entries.note: 'System problems' is probably a typo for 'system prompts'. 'Inherent' is his own framing and is carried over into the proposition.

entries.test: Enterprise surveys from 2024 on adoption barriers, checking whether accuracy and reliability concerns are a leading reason deployments stall.
entries.note: Proving 'precisely because' is hard; surveys of stated barriers are the closest public evidence.

entries.test: Reported AI capital expenditure and investment totals for 2023–2024, checking whether they reach hundreds of billions of dollars.
entries.note: The motive ('speculation that scaling would cure') can't be checked; only the investment amount can.
He says 'new approaches to AI'. The drafter added 'beyond LLMs', which is more specific than his words.
